what: BTSBM-package: Bayesian paired-comparison and ranking models with latent blocks
title: Package 'RBBayes'
text: Description RBBayes provides Bayesian Bradley–Terry Plackett–Luce models one data–model–fit interface. vignette focuses Bradley–Terry stochastic block model (BT–SBM), items similar competitive strength share ordered latent block. model learns block membership, block strength, number occupied blocks jointly. Details Pairwise-comparison data record directional outcomes items: player defeats opponent, judge prefers one object another, one system wins evaluation. classical Bradley–Terry model assigns every item positive strength therefore induces strict order. resolution can fine nearby items credibly separable. BT–SBM instead assigns item \(\) latent block \(z_i\). Items block share strength \(\lambda_{z_i}\); occupied blocks ordered strength. result probabilistic tiered ranking rather forced item--item ordering. Posterior output keeps uncertainty visible distribution number blocks, block-ordered outcome matrix, conditional assignment probabilities, rank intervals. public workflow four stages: prepare data, specify model, set MCMC controls, fit. fit class consumed summaries, plots, diagnostics, predictive-comparison functions. Quick start Authors Lapo Santi Nial Friel. References Bradley, R. . Terry, M. E. (1952). Rank analysis incomplete block designs: . method paired comparisons. Biometrika, 39(3/4), 324–345. Santi, L. Friel, N. (2026). Bradley–Terry stochastic block model. Annals Applied Statistics, 20(2), 1766–1787.
code: wins <- ATP_2000_2025$`2017`$Y_ij diag(wins) <- 0L  pairwise <- as_bt_data(wins) model <- bt_sbm_model(   shape_lambda = 2, rate_lambda = exp(digamma(2)),   item_clustering = gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyper = 0.8) ) fit <- fit_model(   pairwise,   model,   mcmc_control(iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 1) )  pretty_table_K_distribution(fit, p_min = 0) plot_block_adjacency(fit) plot_assignment_probabilities(fit)

what: as_bt_data: Create validated Bradley–Terry pairwise data
title: Package 'RBBayes'
text: Description as_bt_data() converts square directed win-count matrix validated pairwise-data representation used common fitting interface. Usage Arguments Value object class btsbm_pairwise_data. contains validated directed win matrix labels required fitting plotting methods. Details Let \(w_{ij}\) number times item \(\) defeats item \(j\), \(w_{ii}=0\), define \(n_{ij}=w_{ij}+w_{ji}\). RBBayes stores matrix \(\mathbf W=(w_{ij})\) object returned as_bt_data() computes match totals internally. Example vignette uses one synthetic league throughout. contains 18 players generated three strength tiers.
code: as_bt_data(wins, item_labels = NULL) simulation <- sample_from_BTSBM(   n_players = 18,   K = 3,   mean_matches = 8,   p_edge = 0.75,   lambda = c(0.25, 0.9, 2.4),   reverse_lambda = FALSE,   seed = 123 )  player_labels <- paste0("Player_", seq_len(nrow(simulation$w))) pairwise <- as_bt_data(simulation$w, item_labels = player_labels) pairwise$wins[1:6, 1:6] #>          Player_1 Player_2 Player_3 Player_4 Player_5 Player_6 #> Player_1        0        1        0        0        0        0 #> Player_2        5        0        1        6        0        0 #> Player_3        0        6        0        0        5        2 #> Player_4        5        2        0        0        0        0 #> Player_5        0        0        4       12        0        0 #> Player_6        0        0        5        0        5        0

what: bt_sbm_model: Define a Bradley–Terry stochastic block model
title: Package 'RBBayes'
text: Description bt_sbm_model() defines clustered Bradley–Terry model. simple model defined bt_model(). constructors return btsbm_model fitted fit_model(). Usage Arguments Value btsbm_model specification. records scientific choices without starting sampler. Details item block label \(z_i\\{1,\ldots,K\}\) occupied block positive strength \(\lambda_k\). probability win \[ \Pr(\text{ defeats }j\mid x,\lambda) =\frac{\lambda_{z_i}}{\lambda_{z_i}+\lambda_{z_j}}, \] aggregated observation satisfies \[ w_{ij}\mid n_{ij},x,\lambda \sim\operatorname{Binomial}\!\left( n_{ij},\frac{\lambda_{z_i}}{\lambda_{z_i}+\lambda_{z_j}} \right). \] prior \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) named model component rather collection sampler-specific arguments. Examples
code: bt_sbm_model(   shape_lambda = 4,   rate_lambda = exp(digamma(shape_lambda)),   item_clustering = gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyper = 0.5),   latent_strength = NULL,   ability_prior = NULL,   item_prior = NULL ) model_gnedin <- bt_sbm_model(   shape_lambda = 2, rate_lambda = exp(digamma(2)),   item_clustering = gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyper = 0.8) )  model_finite <- bt_sbm_model(   item_clustering = finite_partition(max_clusters = 6) )

what: fit_btsbm: Fit a Bayesian Bradley–Terry or Plackett–Luce model
title: Package 'RBBayes'
text: Description fit_model() common fitting entry point simple clustered Bradley–Terry Plackett–Luce models. Usage Arguments Value object class btsbm_fit. stable draw names allow downstream summary diagnostic functions work across supported models. Details internal BT–SBM kernel alternates three updates. Thurstonian augmentation introduces latent \(Z_{ij}\) variables observed pairs. Item labels updated one time using selected partition prior augmented likelihood. Finally, occupied strengths conjugate Gamma updates. number occupied blocks may change label update, \(K\) sampled rather fixed. Cluster labels permutation-invariant. summaries vignette, draw relabelled decreasing occupied strength: block 1 strongest, block 2 second strongest, forth. Users need call separate relabel step using btsbm_fit functions documented . Example
code: fit_model(data, model, control = mcmc_control()) model <- bt_sbm_model(   shape_lambda = 2, rate_lambda = exp(digamma(2)),   item_clustering = gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyper = 0.8) )  fit <- fit_model(pairwise, model, control) fit #> <btsbm_fit> Bradley-Terry stochastic block model (BT-SBM), items share block strengths  #>   18 items; 200 retained posterior draws. Use summary() for results. str(list(   item_cluster = dim(fit$draws$item_cluster),   n_item_clusters = length(fit$draws$n_item_clusters),   latent_strength = length(fit$draws$latent_strength) )) #> List of 3 #>  $ item_cluster   : int [1:2] 200 18 #>  $ n_item_clusters: int 200 #>  $ latent_strength: int 200

NULL, uses rep(seq_len(K), length.= n_players). mean_matches Positive numeric. Poisson mean match counts present edges. p_edge Numeric [0,1]. Probability unordered pair present topology. lambda Optional positive numeric vector length K. NULL, geometric sequence used: lambda_base * lambda_ratio^(0:(K-1)). lambda_base Positive numeric. Base geometric schedule lambda provided. Default 0.08 (snippet). lambda_ratio Positive numeric. Ratio geometric schedule lambda provided. Default 2.3 (snippet). reverse_lambda Logical. text: list components: N — \(n \times n\) integer matrix symmetric match counts zero diagonal. W — \(n \times n\) integer matrix directed win counts w[, j] + w[j, ] = N[, j]. x — integer vector block labels 1:K. lambda — numeric vector length K used build theta. theta — \(K \times K\) matrix entries \(\theta_{ab} = \lambda_a / (\lambda_a + \lambda_b)\).

title: Sample a Bradley–Terry Stochastic Block Model (BT-SBM) tournament — sample_from_BTSBM
text: workflow : Sample symmetric match-count matrix \(N\) first drawing random subset unordered pairs probability p_edge, assigning selected pair Poisson\((mean\_matches)\) number matches. Compute block--block Bradley–Terry matrix \(\theta = \lambda \mathbf{1}^\top / (\lambda \mathbf{1}^\top + \mathbf{1}\lambda^\top)\). unordered pair \(N_{ij}>0\), draw \(w_{ij} \sim \text{Binomial}(N_{ij}, \theta_{x_i, x_j})\) set \(w_{ji} = N_{ij} - w_{ij}\). default, block labels assigned deterministically rep(seq_len(K), length.= n_players) mirror example, can pass custom label vector via x.
